rows.rootCause: Android 13 runtime notification permission was treated as a manifest declaration.
The case-hold scope is computed dynamically from mutable links (resolveLinkedCaseIds), but the one detach authority treats linkage as a pure relationship edit and has no preservation gate.

Popup parses an invented envelope key. The acceptance spec never opens the popup: it writes the token into storage and sends PRESERVE with PROOVRA_E2E_TEAM_ID directly from the service worker (direct-web-capture.spec.ts:409-449), so the defect is structurally invisible to every existing test.
Tile timing chosen for lazy-load settling only, ignoring the platform capture quota; real-browser acceptance never passed (UC1 doc §K), so it was never observed.
The iOS device shape was never reconciled with the manifest schema; server tests fabricate the device object instead of deriving it from the native payload.
The extension side of the stop handshake was never implemented; the app-side comment (:98-99) assumes it exists.
finalizeSegment's force path passes a literal 0 instead of measuring the segment.

ET-PKG-07 made records private by default and gave reports their own token, but the report template, README and owner UI were not updated for the unpublished state; the public route collapses unpublished into not-found.
The column is named capturedAtUtc but holds server creation time; surfaces label it by its name, and basic-verification.ts invented a 'Declared' semantics for it.
SCREEN_CONTINUOUS_STREAM_BOUNDS.maxSegments / SCREEN_CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_BOUNDS.maxSegments (600) were never reconciled with MAX_EVIDENCE_PARTS (200) introduced by ET-ACQ-07.
Completeness is taken from the native recorder's termination only; upload-side loss is not an input to completeness, and the server cannot see segments that were never declared.
Durability of the streaming session was designed around the React component lifetime, not the foreground-service lifetime.
No logout hook for capture state.
Error from MediaRecorder.stop() treated as ignorable.
UC-0 treats 'server-issued session' as the authority for mode, but the server issues whatever mode the caller requests.
Lifecycle side effects implemented in route handlers instead of the canonical createEvidence service.
Same as UC-ARCH-002 on the completion side: route-resident fan-out.
Byte-write authority has only OWNER and INTAKE_SESSION principals; the integration path was not migrated when ET-UPL-01 was remediated.
Intake records reuse the owner's byte-write and completion authority instead of a session-bound one like UC-0.
resolveCaseRecordAccess synthesizes MEMBER for any access-list grantee; the unlink path relies solely on that role (detach has no record-access check).
Intake/request caseId was designed as metadata; the case-evidence authority has an INTAKE source value with no writer.

The 24h TTL was added to the COUNT (so abandoned reservations free their slot) without adding the matching refusal at COMPLETION, while settlement's 'prior records' cursor assumes every earlier record is already counted.

The idempotency key is per (kind, evidence) forever and the reuse path ignores status; the route's 'dismiss then re-enqueue' assumes a new row will be inserted, but the unique key and the status-blind reuse return the settled row, which the exclusive claim correctly refuses.
The Phase 31.14 bytes proxy predates the 2026-09-29 single byte-release authority and was never folded into it (the redaction derivative was, ET-SEC-26).
The keyframe rendition reuses the video_frame thumbnail sizing, and the same bytes feed OCR.
The deterministic core assumes the whole frame scrolls and OCR is exact; the runtime supplies neither fingerprints nor change-scored frames that the core's safety rules rely on.
Lineage columns were added at UC-0 but producers were not updated to fill them; the observation record type omitted geometry.
UC-0's 'never orphan a pointer' rule was implemented as replace-and-delete rather than versioning; the orchestrator never reconciles the previous run's variant set.
Bounds sized for Phase-31 thumbnails (one per part) were not revisited when UC-4 added many-per-part variants.
Derived-asset and run tables are team-keyed; the personal-owner model was never extended to derivatives.
loadWorkspaces collapses every non-OK outcome to an empty array.
The manifest was designed as a validation input only; no read-model consumes it.
busy() is popup DOM state; the orchestrator is stateless.
Authorize reuses API-only requireAuth, which is designed for XHR callers.
Secret clearing is input-centric.
Shared UC-3 client flow assumes the host process runs during capture, which is false on iOS.
No 'broadcast started' signal from extension to app (broadcastStarted writes nothing and posts nothing, SampleHandler.swift:35-45).
Fallback written as a placeholder.
Error paths of AVAssetWriter not handled.
Android MediaProjection assumption (buffer geometry follows display rotation) carried to ReplayKit.
rows.runtimeEvidenceStatus: source-proven (device behaviour of the attachment per Apple ReplayKit documentation; device confirmation BLOCKED)

rows.rootCause: Lifecycle callbacks not implemented.
The shared continuous screen was designed around a foreground-service Android process that survives app switches.
Legal corpus not extended when UC-2/3/5 shipped.
Two hand-maintained switch tables in shared-runtime were not widened when UC-1..UC-5 added modes; resolveEvidenceAcquisition is not their source.
UC-1/UC-2 stopped at validation; no projection/persistence step for manifest facts was built.
ET-DC-02/03 remediation reworded evidence-acquisition.ts only; copy outside the resolver was not swept.
Capture Environment was designed for in-browser capture and reused unchanged for uploads.
ET-UPL-01 fix moved the bridge to the byte-write authority as the SESSION's actor, not the CALLER; per-route caller checks were added only to create/abort.
UC-1 added OAuth redirect pinning but not the matching CORS/host-permission wiring.
Redaction is a hand-maintained regex list rather than derived from route parameters.
Extension OAuth reuses signJwt but not the session-inventory write that every other login path performs.
ET-DC-06 made the server expiry slide, but the mobile durable record kept the open-time value.
Manual launch ignores project configuration; no assertion on the launched browser identity.
Worker integration suites were written against the API's TEST_DATABASE_URL convention but the worker has no CI step that provides a database.
Harness replaced (c8291b86 → 76fddb72) without updating the CI step that served the old harness.
Commit 5621aeb4 (ET-DC-04) changed isAllowedExtensionRedirect to require an explicit allow-list without updating the harness or the fixture-env scanner.
chrome.runtime.sendMessage does not dispatch to listeners in the sending context; the spec was never executed successfully (memory: 'browser E2E needs a real gesture').
The fingerprint is treated as an opaque signed blob; fileSha256 and part sha256 columns were introduced as 'the' digest and every later reader trusts them.
The projection infers state from custody event TYPES, whose names ('OTS_APPLIED', 'TIMESTAMP_APPLIED') predate the claim/validation vocabularies.
Evidence signing predates the package-seal hardening; the key registry was designed as a convenience lookup, not as the record's identity binding.
The sub-chain was added for concurrency (ET-DC-10) and display, not as a verified structure.
ET-SM-07 added the recheck as a new row beside the existing verdict pipeline instead of as an input to the shared trust decision.
STORED_BYTES_INTEGRITY 'verified_current' is time-window based (INTEGRITY_RECHECK_INTERVAL_DAYS default 30) and maps to the badge 'Verified'; no read path re-hashes.
Finalize treated as one-shot; draft transition bound to create instead of seal.
Session-per-redemption design with no client-held session handle.
Home CTA not reconciled with the registry's own note.
Partial application of the ET-DC-11 fix.

Assumption that secure windows throw.
